nodes.label: STT-GEN-001
nodes.title: Issuance and verification of the full HCERT QR pipeline
nodes.statement: The library SHALL implement issuance (steps 1 to 9) and verification (QR Code Generation section 11) of HCERT QR codes.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-002
nodes.title: Every step callable on its own
nodes.statement: Each pipeline step SHALL be exposed as a separate public operation (payload codec, CBOR, COSE sign/parse, ZLIB, Base45, HC1 prefix) as well as through the end-to-end issuer and verifier, so that integrators can substitute or inspect any stage.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-003
nodes.title: Payload-agnostic core
nodes.statement: The modules for steps 3 to 9 SHALL NOT depend on any payload logical model. Payloads SHALL be plugged in through a PayloadCodec registered against a subclaim.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-004
nodes.title: Kotlin first, for JVM, Android and Node
nodes.statement: The first implementation SHALL be a Kotlin Multiplatform library with all pipeline logic in common code. It SHALL ship for three targets: JVM (Java 11+), Android, and Node.js (Kotlin/JS IR, published to npm with an @JsExport facade and generated TypeScript declarations). Other KMP targets MAY follow.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-005
nodes.title: Rust second, for WebAssembly
nodes.statement: The second implementation SHALL be a Rust library meeting this same requirement set. It SHALL build for wasm32 as a WebAssembly component implementing the WIT worlds in api/wit, and SHALL be transpiled with jco into an npm package usable from Node.js and browsers. A native crate SHALL also be published. The codec module SHOULD build without std (with alloc).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-006
nodes.title: Kotlin and Rust behave the same
nodes.statement: The Kotlin and Rust libraries SHALL expose the same conceptual operations, the same configuration knobs and the same failure taxonomy, with idiomatic naming in each language, and SHALL pass the same conformance vectors.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-007
nodes.title: HCERT Specification is authoritative
nodes.statement: Where the QR Code Generation walkthrough and the HCERT Specification differ, the library SHALL follow the HCERT Specification. Each release SHALL state which HCERT Specification version and which smart-trust IG version it implements (currently 1.1.1 and 1.7.5).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-008
nodes.title: CBOR is the wire format; JSON is optional
nodes.statement: The library SHALL work entirely on in-memory structures and CBOR. It SHALL NOT need a JSON representation to issue or verify. A JSON view of payloads MAY be provided for display and debugging.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-009
nodes.title: Raw transport besides QR
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL be able to return the signed COSE_Sign1 bytes without the barcode encodings, and the verifier SHALL accept COSE_Sign1 bytes directly, for 8-bit-safe transports (NFC, Bluetooth, app-to-app).

nodes.label: STT-GEN-010
nodes.title: API defined first, in WIT
nodes.statement: The library API SHALL be defined in WIT (api/wit) and reviewed before implementation. The WIT SHALL be the contract both implementations follow: Rust exports it from its WebAssembly component, and Kotlin follows it through documented mapping rules. Each WIT item SHALL cite the requirement(s) it implements. Breaking WIT changes SHALL bump the package version.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-011
nodes.title: Same JavaScript surface from Kotlin/JS and Rust/WASM
nodes.statement: The Node.js packages built from Kotlin/JS and from the Rust WebAssembly component SHALL expose the same TypeScript surface: the declarations jco generates from the WIT (api/generated/ts). The Kotlin/JS declarations SHALL type-check against it.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-012
nodes.title: Synchronous core with no I/O
nodes.statement: The pipeline core SHALL do no network or file I/O and SHALL NOT read an ambient clock. Trust material SHALL be loaded into a trust store by the host, and the current time SHALL be passed as an argument. Fetching, caching and refreshing trust lists SHALL live in separate, platform-specific modules.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-013
nodes.title: Types and schemas trace to open standards
nodes.statement: Every data type in the API contract, wire schema and payload models SHALL trace to an openly available standard: IETF CBOR/CDDL (RFC 8949, RFC 8610) for the wire format, HL7 FHIR data types and W3C XSD datatypes for payload elements, W3C JSON-LD and SHACL for payload semantics, ITU-T X.680 for certificates, and I-JSON (RFC 7493) for JSON files. Paywalled standards SHALL NOT be used as type or schema references.

nodes.label: STT-GEN-014
nodes.title: Kotlin API skeleton generated from the WIT
nodes.statement: The Kotlin API (types and interfaces, no behaviour) SHALL be generated from the WIT contract by tools/wit2kotlin.py, following the WIT to Kotlin mapping rules in api/README.md, into a Kotlin Multiplatform module targeting the JVM and Node.js. Kotlin implementations SHALL implement the generated interfaces. CI SHALL fail when the generated skeleton is out of date with the WIT or does not compile.

nodes.label: STT-SEL-001
nodes.title: Built-in subclaim registry
nodes.statement: The library SHALL ship a subclaim registry containing 1 (HCertDCC), 3 (DDCCCoreDataSetVS), 4 (DDCCCoreDataSetTR), 5 (VHL URI), -6 (DVCMin) and -7 (MedicationTreatmentLineMin), each with its status (Assigned, Proposed, Development range) and logical-model canonical URL.

nodes.label: STT-SEL-002
nodes.title: Registry is extensible
nodes.statement: Integrators SHALL be able to register more subclaims and their codecs, and override the defaults, at runtime, without forking the library.

nodes.label: STT-SEL-003
nodes.title: Development-range subclaims need explicit opt-in
nodes.statement: The registry SHALL classify subclaims >= 0 as WHO-reserved and negative subclaims as development range. The issuer SHALL refuse to issue a development-range subclaim unless the issuer policy explicitly allows it. The subclaim number used for a payload type SHALL be configuration, not a constant in a codec, so that DVC can move from -6 to an assigned number without an API break.

nodes.label: STT-SEL-004
nodes.title: Exactly one payload when issuing
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL emit an hcert (-260) map with exactly one entry. The verifier SHALL fail verification with MultipleSubclaims when there is more than one entry, and with HcertMissing when there is none.

nodes.label: STT-SEL-006
nodes.title: Trust domain codes come from the value set
nodes.statement: Trust domain codes (currently DDCC, IPS-PILGRIMAGE, PH4H, ICVP) SHALL be treated as data loaded from, or checked against, the GDHCN Trust Domain value set. They SHALL NOT be a closed enum.

nodes.label: STT-PAY-001
nodes.title: Typed DVCMin model
nodes.statement: The library SHALL provide a typed DVCMin payload with the short element names and cardinalities of the logical model: n 1..1, dob 1..1, s 1..1, nt 1..1, id 0..1, dt 0..1, gn 0..1, vx 1..1, v 1..1, and a PayloadCodec for it.

nodes.label: STT-PAY-002
nodes.title: Typed DVCMinVaccineDetails model
nodes.statement: The library SHALL provide the vx structure with vp 1..1, dv 1..1, cn 0..1, is 0..1 and bo 1..1.

nodes.label: STT-PAY-003
nodes.title: One immunization event per DVC
nodes.statement: A DVCMin SHALL carry exactly one vx. The library SHALL provide a helper that turns one visit with N administered vaccines into N payloads, one per vaccine, and so N certificates.

nodes.label: STT-PAY-004
nodes.title: Issuer-or-clinician invariant
nodes.statement: Validation SHALL fail a DVCMin whose vx has neither is nor cn (invariant must-have-issuer-or-clinician-name). The issuer SHALL NOT sign a payload that fails validation.

nodes.label: STT-PAY-005
nodes.title: Subjects with no identity document
nodes.statement: The DVCMin model SHALL allow id and dt to be absent and SHALL support gn (parent or guardian) for subjects such as newborns.

nodes.label: STT-PAY-007
nodes.title: Nationality is ISO 3166-1 alpha-3
nodes.statement: Validation SHALL check that nt is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code, including user-assigned codes such as XXA, which is used for testing.

nodes.label: STT-PAY-008
nodes.title: Preserve unknown payload elements
nodes.statement: Decoding a typed payload SHALL keep unknown elements and SHALL NOT fail because of them, so that newer template versions (v) can still be read and displayed.

nodes.label: STT-PAY-009
nodes.title: Other payloads
nodes.statement: Subclaim 5 SHALL have a typed codec holding a URI string. Subclaims 1, 3, 4 and -7 SHALL at least be issuable and verifiable as raw CBOR payloads. Typed codecs for them MAY follow.

nodes.label: STT-PAY-010
nodes.title: Payload models derived from FHIR logical models
nodes.statement: Payload schemas SHALL be derived mechanically from the published FHIR logical models, not written by hand: a JSON-LD 1.1 context that maps the payload's short element names to IRIs, SHACL shapes for cardinality, primitive patterns, invariants and bindings, and CDDL for the CBOR encoding. Inputs SHALL be pinned to a source commit. Typed payload codecs SHALL be checked against these derived schemas.

nodes.label: STT-CWT-001
nodes.title: Integer claim keys
nodes.statement: The CWT claim set SHALL use the integer keys 1 (iss), 6 (iat), 4 (exp) and -260 (hcert). The hcert map SHALL use integer subclaim keys. The quoted keys in the documentation ("1", "-260", "-6") are JSON notation only and SHALL NOT be emitted as text keys.

nodes.label: STT-CWT-002
nodes.title: NumericDate integers
nodes.statement: iat and exp SHALL be encoded as integer NumericDate (seconds since the epoch). The decoder SHOULD accept floating-point NumericDate and truncate it.

nodes.label: STT-CWT-003
nodes.title: Expiry is mandatory on issuance
nodes.statement: The issuer API SHALL require an explicit validity (exp, or a validity period) and SHALL have no default of "never expires". exp is the only revocation mechanism.

nodes.label: STT-CWT-004
nodes.title: Validity inside the DSC validity
nodes.statement: Before signing, the issuer SHALL check that iat is not before the DSC notBefore and exp is not after the DSC notAfter, and SHALL refuse to sign otherwise.

nodes.label: STT-CWT-005
nodes.title: iss is an optional alpha-2 string
nodes.statement: iss SHALL be optional and SHALL be encoded as a text string. When present, the issuer SHALL require two upper-case letters, the alpha-2 form used in iss and in the DSC's X.509 C attribute.

nodes.label: STT-CWT-006
nodes.title: Preserve unknown claims
nodes.statement: The decoder SHALL keep CWT claims it does not recognise and expose them to the caller.

nodes.label: STT-CBR-001
nodes.title: Deterministic CBOR on encode
nodes.statement: The encoder SHALL produce deterministic CBOR (RFC 8949 section 4.2.1 core deterministic encoding). For the HCERT key sets this matches the RFC 7049 canonical ordering the reference script uses. Same input gives same bytes, in both languages.

nodes.label: STT-CBR-002
nodes.title: NFC normalisation
nodes.statement: The encoder SHOULD NFC-normalise text strings. The decoder SHALL accept strings that are not normalised, and comparison helpers SHALL behave as if both sides were normalised to NFC.

nodes.label: STT-CBR-003
nodes.title: Bounded CBOR decoding
nodes.statement: The CBOR decoder SHALL enforce configurable limits on nesting depth, item count and string/byte-string length, and SHALL reject malformed or truncated input with a typed error, without panicking or throwing unchecked exceptions.

nodes.label: STT-CBR-004
nodes.title: Wire format specified in CDDL
nodes.statement: The CBOR wire format (COSE_Sign1, protected header, CWT claim set, hcert map and payloads) SHALL be specified in CDDL (RFC 8610), and encoders SHALL produce data that validates against it. The envelope SHALL be hand-written from the HCERT Specification; payload rules SHALL be generated from the logical models (STT-PAY-010).

nodes.label: STT-COS-001
nodes.title: COSE_Sign1 structure
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL emit 18([protected bstr, unprotected map, payload bstr, signature bstr]). The verifier SHALL accept the tagged form and SHOULD also accept an untagged COSE_Sign1 array.

nodes.label: STT-COS-002
nodes.title: Both ES256 and PS256
nodes.statement: The library SHALL implement signing and verification for ES256 (alg -7, ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256) and PS256 (alg -37, RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256, MGF1 SHA-256, salt length 32, modulus at least 2048 bits).

nodes.label: STT-COS-003
nodes.title: kid placement
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL put alg and kid in the protected header. The verifier SHALL accept a kid in either the protected or the unprotected header, and SHALL use the protected one when both are present.

nodes.label: STT-COS-004
nodes.title: Sig_structure
nodes.statement: The signature input SHALL be the CBOR encoding of ["Signature1", protected header bytes exactly as transmitted, empty external_aad, payload bytes]. The verifier SHALL use the received protected bytes and SHALL NOT re-encode the decoded header.

nodes.label: STT-COS-005
nodes.title: Fixed-width r||s ECDSA signatures
nodes.statement: ES256 signatures SHALL be carried as 64-byte r||s. The library SHALL convert from and to the ASN.1 DER form returned or expected by platform crypto APIs (JCA, Android Keystore, PKCS#11, RustCrypto). The verifier SHALL reject an ES256 signature that is not exactly 64 bytes.

nodes.label: STT-COS-006
nodes.title: No private keys required in-process
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL NOT need access to private key material: issuance is prepare, then the caller signs the returned bytes by any means (HSM, KMS, PKCS#11, Android Keystore, WebCrypto), then finish (STT-ISS-004). A software ES256 and PS256 signer SHALL be provided for tests only, in the testkit module.

nodes.label: STT-KID-001
nodes.title: kid derivation
nodes.statement: kid SHALL be the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the DER-encoded DSC. The issuer SHALL derive it from the Signer's DSC, not take it from the caller.

nodes.label: STT-KID-002
nodes.title: kid is a lookup hint, not unique
nodes.statement: Trust-list lookup by kid SHALL return every matching DSC, and the verifier SHALL try each candidate until one verifies. A kid match alone SHALL NOT count as authentication.

nodes.label: STT-KID-003
nodes.title: kid text forms
nodes.statement: Kid SHALL convert to and from hex, standard base64 and URL-safe base64. Trust-list matching SHALL compare the kid bytes, not their text form.

nodes.label: STT-ZIP-001
nodes.title: ZLIB/Deflate after signing
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL compress the COSE_Sign1 bytes with ZLIB (RFC 1950) using Deflate (RFC 1951) after signing. The verifier SHALL decompress before parsing COSE.

nodes.label: STT-ZIP-002
nodes.title: Decompression bomb protection
nodes.statement: Inflation SHALL stop with a typed error once the output exceeds a configurable limit (DecodeLimits.maxInflatedBytes).

nodes.label: STT-B45-001
nodes.title: Base45 per RFC 9285
nodes.statement: Base45 encoding and decoding SHALL follow RFC 9285, the published form of the draft the IG cites.

nodes.label: STT-B45-002
nodes.title: Strict Base45 decoding
nodes.statement: The decoder SHALL reject characters outside the 45-character alphabet, a dangling single character, and triplets or pairs whose value overflows (above 65535, or above 255 for a trailing pair).

nodes.label: STT-HC1-001
nodes.title: HC1 prefix
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL prefix the Base45 string with "HC1:". The verifier SHALL require a context identifier matching HC[1-9A-Z]: and strip it. It SHALL report any identifier other than HC1 as an unsupported version, distinct from malformed input.

nodes.label: STT-QR-001
nodes.title: QR-ready HC1 output; no QR encoding in the library
nodes.statement: The HC1 string SHALL consist only of characters in the QR Alphanumeric set (the Base45 alphabet and the "HC1:" prefix), so that integrators can encode it as a single Alphanumeric-mode segment with error correction Q using any QR encoder. The libraries SHALL NOT encode or render QR symbols.

nodes.label: STT-QR-005
nodes.title: Camera scanning out of scope
nodes.statement: Decoding QR images from a camera or file is out of scope for the core libraries. The verifier entry point SHALL be the scanned text (HC1 string) or raw COSE bytes.

nodes.label: STT-VER-001
nodes.title: Verification order
nodes.statement: The verifier SHALL run the QR Code Generation section 11 sequence in order: prefix, Base45, inflate, COSE parse, header validation, trust lookup by kid, signature verification, EKU check, CWT decode and time checks, subclaim dispatch, business rules.

nodes.label: STT-VER-002
nodes.title: No payload access before the signature is verified
nodes.statement: The API SHALL make the payload and claims reachable only through a successful verification result type. Code that inspects an unverified payload SHALL go through an explicitly named unsafe or diagnostic call.

nodes.label: STT-VER-003
nodes.title: Defensive protected-header parsing
nodes.statement: Before the signature is checked, the verifier SHALL validate the types and lengths in the protected header: alg is a supported integer, kid is a byte string of the expected length, and no duplicate labels. It SHALL fail closed on anything unexpected.

nodes.label: STT-VER-004
nodes.title: EKU check against certificate type
nodes.statement: If the matching DSC has an Extended Key Usage extension with any of 1.3.6.1.4.1.1847.2021.1.1 (test), .1.2 (vaccinations) or .1.3 (recovery), the verifier SHALL check it against the certificate type of the payload: DVC (-6) and DDCC VS (3) are vaccinations, DDCC TR (4) is test, and a DCC (1) is the type of its single v, t or r entry. A DSC with no such extension SHALL be accepted for any type.

nodes.label: STT-VER-005
nodes.title: Time checks with an injected clock
nodes.statement: The verifier SHALL reject a certificate whose exp is in the past, and one whose iat is in the future beyond a configurable clock-skew tolerance. The current time SHALL be passed in by the caller (now), never read from an ambient clock.

nodes.label: STT-VER-006
nodes.title: Trust-list presence is the DSC validity check
nodes.statement: The verifier SHALL NOT need CRL or OCSP access. A DSC is valid if it is on the current trust list. The verifier SHOULD also check the DSC's X.509 validity period against the injected clock.

nodes.label: STT-VER-007
nodes.title: Dispatch to logical model, then business rules
nodes.statement: After verification the verifier SHALL decode the hcert entry with the codec registered for its subclaim, falling back to RawPayload. It SHALL then run any registered BusinessRuleHooks and attach their outcomes to the result.

nodes.label: STT-VER-008
nodes.title: Typed verification result and failure taxonomy
nodes.statement: A certificate failing verification SHALL produce a Failed result, not an exception or panic. Failed results SHALL name the step that failed and a reason from a closed set shared by both languages: BadPrefix, UnsupportedContextVersion, Base45Invalid, InflateFailed, LimitExceeded, CoseMalformed, HeaderInvalid, UnsupportedAlgorithm, KidNotFound, SignatureInvalid, KeyUsageMismatch, Expired, NotYetValid, HcertMissing, MultipleSubclaims, PayloadInvalid. Exceptions or errors SHALL be reserved for programming errors and infrastructure failures.

nodes.label: STT-VER-009
nodes.title: Fully offline verification
nodes.statement: Given a cached or static trust list, verification SHALL need no network access.

nodes.label: STT-VER-011
nodes.title: Unverified read for triage
nodes.statement: The verifier SHALL offer an explicitly named unverified read (read-unverified) that decodes an HC1 string up to and including the payload without any trust lookup or signature check, for display and triage where verification is not possible, such as a community health worker offline at a household (journey J2). Its result type SHALL be distinct from a verified result, SHALL carry the kid and the claims it found, and SHALL state that nothing in it is verified. It SHALL apply the same decode limits as verify.

nodes.label: STT-TRU-001
nodes.title: Trust store
nodes.statement: Trust material SHALL be held in a trust store that the host fills with DSCs it has obtained, and that returns every trusted DSC matching a kid. The store SHALL do no network or file I/O (STT-GEN-012).

nodes.label: STT-TRU-002
nodes.title: GDHCN DID trustlist v2 documents
nodes.statement: The trust store SHALL load GDHCN DID trustlist v2 documents, embedded and reference variants, reading DSCs from verificationMethod publicKeyJwk (x5c) with the kid as the fragment. Fetching the documents, caching them and checking their proofs are the host's.

nodes.label: STT-TRU-005
nodes.title: Static trust lists
nodes.statement: The trust store SHALL load DSCs from PEM and DER, for tests, pinned bilateral or national lists, and fully offline deployments.

nodes.label: STT-VHL-001
nodes.title: VHL payload in the SMART Health Links payload format
nodes.statement: The library SHALL model the VHL payload as the SMART Health Links payload format that IHE VHL reuses: url (required, https), key (required, 43 base64url characters encoding 32 bytes), exp (optional integer, epoch seconds), flag (optional; the letters L and P in alphabetical order), label (optional, at most 80 characters), v (optional integer, default 1) and extension.fhirBaseUrl (optional). Validation SHALL report each violation. The single-file U flag is out of scope and SHALL be reported as unsupported.

nodes.label: STT-VHL-002
nodes.title: VHL payload at HCERT key 5 as a CBOR map
nodes.statement: The issuer SHALL carry the VHL payload at HCERT claim -260 key 5 as a CBOR map with text keys, exp and v as CBOR integers. The verifier SHALL read key 5 as that map, and SHALL also accept a vhlink:/ text string there, so that VHLs built to IHE ITI-YY3 still verify.

nodes.label: STT-VHL-003
nodes.title: vhlink:/ text form
nodes.statement: The library SHALL convert a VHL payload to and from its text form: the minified JSON, base64url-encoded without padding (RFC 4648), prefixed with vhlink:/.

nodes.label: STT-VHL-004
nodes.title: VHL key generation
nodes.statement: The library SHALL generate a VHL key as 32 bytes from the platform's cryptographically secure random generator, encoded as 43 base64url characters.

nodes.label: STT-VHL-005
nodes.title: ITI-YY5 manifest request
nodes.statement: The library SHALL build the ITI-YY5 Retrieve Manifest request from a VHL payload: POST to <base>/List/_search (accepting a manifest URL of either the List?... or the List/_search?... form), Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded, body holding the manifest URL's search parameters (_id, code, status and patient.identifier required; _include=List:item optional) plus recipient (required), passcode (required when, and only when, the payload's flag has P) and embeddedLengthMax (optional). It SHALL refuse a payload whose URL lacks a required parameter. Sending the request is the host's.

nodes.label: STT-VHL-006
nodes.title: ITI-YY5 manifest response
nodes.statement: The library SHALL read the ITI-YY5 response, a FHIR searchset Bundle: the List with search.mode match and, when the Include DocumentReference option was used, the DocumentReferences with search.mode include. For each document it SHALL return the attachment URL and the decrypted content type (attachment.contentType); for List items whose DocumentReference is not included it SHALL return the reference for the host to read.

nodes.label: STT-VHL-007
nodes.title: Document encryption: JWE dir / A256GCM
nodes.statement: Document binaries SHALL be encrypted and decrypted as JWE Compact Serialization (RFC 7516) with alg dir and enc A256GCM (RFC 7518), the VHL key as the content key and the protected header as additional authenticated data, following SMART Health Links. Decryption SHALL refuse any other alg or enc, SHALL accept zip DEF, and SHALL fail on a bad tag. Encryption SHALL set cty to the document's content type.

nodes.label: STT-VHL-008
nodes.title: Receiver authentication: HTTP Message Signatures
nodes.statement: For the ITI-YY5 HTTP Message Signatures option the library SHALL compute Content-Digest (RFC 9530, sha-256, Structured Field byte sequence) and the RFC 9421 signature base over @method, @path, @authority, content-type and content-digest with created, keyid and alg parameters, return the bytes for the host to sign with the receiver's key, and assemble the Signature-Input and Signature headers from the result. For ecdsa-p256-sha256 the signature SHALL be the 64-byte r||s; a DER signature SHALL be converted.

nodes.label: STT-VHL-009
nodes.title: VHL expiry
nodes.statement: Validating a VHL payload against a caller-supplied now SHALL report an expired link when the payload's exp has passed, in addition to the HCERT exp check made by the verifier.

nodes.label: STT-VHL-010
nodes.title: VHL with no I/O in the library
nodes.statement: The VHL functions SHALL do no network, file or clock access: the host sends the ITI-YY5 request and the ITI-68 document GETs over mutual TLS, holds the receiver's signing key, and logs AuditEvents. The library builds, parses, signs-by-proxy and decrypts.

nodes.label: STT-ISS-003
nodes.title: Test keys never in production artifacts
nodes.statement: Fixed test keys and test PKI (such as the XXA SCA and DSC) SHALL only ship in the testkit module. Production modules SHALL NOT contain or accept them by default.

nodes.label: STT-ISS-004
nodes.title: Two-phase signing
nodes.statement: Issuance SHALL be two-phase: prepare returns the exact bytes to sign (the Sig_structure), the caller signs them by any means, including asynchronous ones such as WebCrypto or a remote KMS, and finish assembles the certificate and returns the HC1 string and the COSE bytes. For ES256, finish SHALL accept r||s or DER and SHALL always emit r||s.

nodes.label: STT-SEC-001
nodes.title: No payload content in logs
nodes.statement: The libraries SHALL NOT log payload content, HC1 strings or decoded claims at any default log level. A QR code holds readable personal data.

nodes.label: STT-SEC-002
nodes.title: Vetted crypto backends
nodes.statement: Cryptography SHALL use platform or vetted libraries: JCA/BouncyCastle or Android Keystore for Kotlin JVM/Android, RustCrypto (p256, rsa, sha2) or ring/aws-lc-rs for Rust. Signature verification SHALL be constant-time where the backend allows. The libraries SHALL NOT contain their own implementations of cryptographic primitives.

nodes.label: STT-NFR-001
nodes.title: Versioning and spec traceability
nodes.statement: Releases SHALL follow semantic versioning. A change to the wire format or to subclaim defaults SHALL be a major or minor version change, as documented in a changelog that cites the smart-trust change (changes.md entry) it implements.

nodes.label: STT-NFR-002
nodes.title: Distribution
nodes.statement: The Kotlin library SHALL be published to Maven Central (JVM, Android AAR) and to npm (Kotlin/JS). The Rust library SHALL be published to crates.io, and its jco-transpiled WebAssembly component to npm. All coordinates are still to be chosen.

nodes.label: STT-TST-001
nodes.title: PR 129 example as a conformance vector
nodes.statement: Both libraries SHALL verify the two HC1 strings in dvc-qr-example-XXA.json against dvc-qr-example-XXA-dsc.pem, with the clock fixed inside 2026-09-29T08:30Z to 2027-09-29T08:30Z. Each SHALL give kid WHM+BYqqZiE=, subclaim -6, and payloads equal to those in the JSON. The committed files SHALL be used as-is; they SHALL NOT be regenerated.

nodes.label: STT-TST-002
nodes.title: Byte-exact CBOR vector
nodes.statement: Encoding the PR 129 example claim sets with deterministic CBOR SHALL give exactly the payload bytes inside the committed COSE_Sign1: 210 bytes for hepb1 and 209 for bcg. Signed, deflated and HC1 sizes SHALL NOT be asserted exactly, because signatures are randomized.

nodes.label: STT-TST-003
nodes.title: Cross-implementation interoperability
nodes.statement: Certificates issued by each library (ES256 and PS256) SHALL verify in the other library and in the smart-trust reference script's verify routine. Certificates issued by the reference script SHALL verify in both libraries.

nodes.label: STT-TST-004
nodes.title: Negative vectors
nodes.statement: The shared vector set SHALL include failing cases with the expected failure reason for each: tampered payload, tampered protected header, wrong or unknown kid, duplicate kid with only the second DSC valid, a DER-encoded ES256 signature, expired, iat before the DSC validity, EKU mismatch, missing or unsupported prefix (HC2:), invalid Base45, decompression bomb, deeply nested CBOR, multiple subclaims, and a DVC without is or cn.

nodes.label: STT-TST-005
nodes.title: Language-neutral vector format
nodes.statement: Conformance vectors SHALL be stored once, in a language-neutral format (JSON plus PEM), in this repository, and loaded by both test suites.

nodes.label: STT-TST-006
nodes.title: Fuzzing of decoders
nodes.statement: The Base45, ZLIB, CBOR, COSE and full verifier entry points SHALL be fuzzed in CI (cargo-fuzz for Rust, Jazzer or kotlinx-fuzz for Kotlin). No input may crash them, hang them, or exceed DecodeLimits.

nodes.label: STT-TST-007
nodes.title: One TypeScript conformance suite for both Node packages
nodes.statement: A single TypeScript test suite, type-checked against api/generated/ts and driven by the shared vectors, SHALL run in CI against both the Kotlin/JS npm package and the jco-transpiled Rust component, and SHALL pass on both.

nodes.label: STT-TST-008
nodes.title: Schema checks against the vectors
nodes.statement: CI SHALL validate every conformance vector against the CDDL (COSE_Sign1, protected header, CWT claims) and its payload against the SHACL shapes through the JSON-LD context. It SHALL also check that mutated payloads (invariant broken, bad FHIR date, missing required element, bad FHIR id) are rejected and that valid variants (cn only, partial date) are accepted, by both CDDL and SHACL.

nodes.label: OI-01
nodes.title: Reference script output is not reproducible byte for byte
nodes.text: QR Code Generation 12 and 13 say the script "regenerates the example above byte for byte". It does not. The DSC is signed by the SCA, and the COSE_Sign1 by the DSC, using randomized ECDSA, so every run produces a different DSC, a different kid and different HC1 strings. Running the script at PR head 50bcb25 twice produced kids ZfzK2Csfpsk= and 2sMkNOHFctA=, against WHM+BYqqZiE= in the PR, and different HC1 strings on every run. The committed artefacts are internally consistent: both committed HC1 strings verify against the committed DSC and the kid matches. The sizes in 12.5 are not stable either: the deflated size came out as 283 bytes instead of 282, and the HC1 length as 429 characters instead of 427.
nodes.hint: Either use RFC 6979 deterministic ECDSA for both signatures, or reword the claim to "regenerates an equivalent example" and treat the committed JSON and PEM as the normative test vector. The library requirements assume the committed artefacts are the vector (STT-TST-001).

nodes.label: QR §12
nodes.title: 12. Worked example — a newborn birth dose DVC

nodes.label: OI-02
nodes.title: One payload per hcert, or several?
nodes.text: QR Code Generation 2 and 4 say an HCERT carries exactly one payload and that -260 is a "map whose single key is the subclaim". HCERT Specification 3.2.7 says "Several different types of health certificate MAY exist under the same claim", and the HCert logical model makes every subclaim 0..1, so it does not rule out more than one. The verifier behaviour for several entries is not specified.
nodes.hint: State in hcert_spec 3.2.7 whether more than one subclaim per hcert is allowed and how a verifier treats it.

nodes.label: OI-03
nodes.title: EKU certificate type for non-DCC payloads is undefined
nodes.text: Appendix A.2 defines EKU OIDs for test, vaccinations and recovery, and QR Code Generation 11 step 7 says to check the EKU "against the certificate type". There is no mapping from subclaims 3, 4, 5, -6 or -7 to a certificate type. DVC (-6) is presumably "vaccinations". VHL (5) has no obvious type.
nodes.hint: Add a subclaim-to-certificate-type table, or use the GDHCN Key Usage value set.

nodes.label: OI-04
nodes.title: Base45 reference points at an expired Internet-Draft
nodes.text: Both pages cite draft-faltstrom-base45. That draft was published as RFC 9285, which should be the reference.

nodes.label: OI-05
nodes.title: CBOR reference RFC 7049 is obsoleted by RFC 8949
nodes.text: Neither page says whether issuers should use deterministic encoding, or which rules. The reference script uses length-first canonical ordering (RFC 7049 section 3.9). For the integer and short text keys used here that gives the same order as RFC 8949 core deterministic encoding, but that is luck, not a rule.

nodes.label: OI-06
nodes.title: Subclaim 5 is called VHL in one place and SHL in another
nodes.text: QR Code Generation 2.1 and the HCert logical model describe subclaim 5 as the URI of a Verifiable Health Link. HCERT Specification 3.2.7.1.5, which is the authoritative list, describes it as Smart Health Link (SHL) and links the SMART Health Links spec. The two define different URI schemes and payloads.
nodes.hint: Raised as WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust#130: 3.2.7.1.5 becomes Verifiable Health Link (IHE ITI VHL, SHL payload format), and the HCert model types key 5 as the trust-phw VerifiableHealthLinkPayload, carried as a CBOR map. The library follows that (STT-VHL-002).

nodes.label: OI-07
nodes.title: iss is a string in the spec but a Coding in the logical model
nodes.text: The CWTPayload logical model types claim 1 as Coding. HCERT 3.2.4 and RFC 8392 type it as a string.

nodes.label: OI-08
nodes.title: Logical model link in hcert_spec uses a different case
nodes.text: hcert_spec.md links StructureDefinition-hcert.html. The resource id is HCert, so the page is StructureDefinition-HCert.html, which is the link QR Code Generation 2.1 uses. On case-sensitive hosting the lowercase link breaks.

nodes.label: OI-09
nodes.title: DVC subclaim -6 is in the development range
nodes.text: The number "is not guaranteed to be stable". The library must not bake -6 into its wire format, and has to be able to move DVC to a WHO-assigned number without a breaking API change.

nodes.label: OI-10
nodes.title: Deployed section anchors and preview paths need checking
nodes.text: The ci and published URLs for PR 129 content, and every section anchor, are computed (see sources.yaml) and cannot be checked until the PR is merged and deployed. Re-run tools/build_kg.py --check-links after deployment.

nodes.label: OI-12
nodes.title: Base64 variant of kid in the DID trustlist is unspecified
nodes.text: The DID trustlist uses a "base64 encoded key id" as the verification method fragment and as JWK kid. It does not say whether that is standard or URL-safe base64, or whether padding is kept. Standard and URL-safe base64 differ on '+' and '/', and the PR example kid WHM+BYqqZiE= contains '+'.

nodes.label: OI-13
nodes.title: Mapping between GDHCN participant codes (alpha-3) and iss (alpha-2)
nodes.text: Participant codes are ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, while iss and the X.509 C attribute use alpha-2. The test pair XXA/XX is user-assigned and not a formal ISO mapping. A verifier narrowing trust-list lookups by iss needs an authoritative mapping.

nodes.label: OI-14
nodes.title: Package coordinates and licence for the libraries
nodes.text: Maven group / Kotlin package root and crate names are placeholders. The natural reverse-DNS root, int.who, cannot be used because `int` is a reserved Java keyword. The licence has not been chosen.

nodes.label: OI-15
nodes.title: Asynchronous crypto and I/O across the WIT boundary
nodes.text: WASI 0.2 component calls are synchronous. WebCrypto (the natural crypto backend for Kotlin/JS on Node and browsers) is promise-based, as are remote KMS signers and HTTP fetches. The design avoids async callbacks into the host: signing is two-phase and trust lists are loaded by the host. The Rust component verifies with in-WASM RustCrypto, so verify stays synchronous. Kotlin/JS must either use Node's synchronous `crypto` module (Node only) or expose a Promise-returning verify, which would diverge from the jco surface. Decide before implementation; revisit when WASI 0.3 async is stable.

nodes.label: OI-16
nodes.title: WIT type-system limits
nodes.text: WIT has no recursive types, so generic CBOR crosses as encoded bytes and only DVCMin and VHL are typed records. s64 becomes bigint in JavaScript, so it is used only for NumericDate, and subclaim numbers are s32. result<T, E> is thrown as ComponentError by jco, so APIs whose failures are expected (verify) return a variant instead.

nodes.label: OI-17
nodes.title: The example issues an abstract logical model
nodes.text: In smart-trust-phw, DVCMin and DVCMinVaccineDetails are declared abstract (^abstract = true). Only DVCMinPreQual and DVCMinVaccineDetailsPreQual are concrete. The HCert logical model puts DVCMin at subclaim -6, and the PR 129 example issues a DVCMin with ICD-11 codes. So no concrete model exists for a non-PreQual DVC: either DVCMin should not be abstract, or a concrete ICD-11 profile is needed.

nodes.label: OI-18
nodes.title: Sex binding in DVCMin points at a CodeSystem, not a ValueSet
nodes.text: DVCMin.s is bound (extensible) to $GENDER, which smart-trust-phw aliases to http://hl7.org/fhir/administrative-gender, the CodeSystem URL. A binding must reference a ValueSet: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/administrative-gender.

nodes.label: OI-19
nodes.title: Upstream home for the CDDL and JSON-LD artefacts
nodes.text: The HCERT envelope CDDL (api/cddl/hcert.cddl) belongs in WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust next to the HCERT Specification, which owns the wire format. The payload JSON-LD context, SHACL and CDDL belong with their logical models in smart-trust-phw, ideally generated by the IG build and published at the canonical URL. They are drafted here until upstream adopts them.

nodes.label: OI-20
nodes.title: CDDL validator deviations (cddl-rs / pycddl)
nodes.text: The only Python CDDL validator, pycddl (wrapping the Rust cddl crate), deviates from RFC 8610 in four ways found here: .cbor inside arrays is applied to the wrong items; .regexp is not implicitly anchored; escaped regex classes such as \s are treated as literals; and map closure is not enforced across group-choice alternatives. The CDDL files stay spec-correct, and tools/check_models.py works around the first three. The schema avoids relying on the fourth. Cross-check with a second validator (e.g. cddlc) before upstreaming.

nodes.label: OI-21
nodes.title: IHE ITI-YY3 puts a vhlink:/ string at HCERT key 5; ITI-YY4 reads an object
nodes.text: ITI-YY3 step 5 base64url-encodes the minified payload JSON, prefixes it with vhlink:/ and puts that text at claim -260 key 5. ITI-YY4 step 8 and its example read key 5 as a decoded object. Text-in-CBOR also costs about a third of the QR: on the ITI-YY3 example the string form is ~609 HC1 characters against ~422 for a CBOR map.
nodes.hint: Patch prepared for the IHE editors (upstream/ihe-iti-vhl/): for the HCERT carrier key 5 is the payload as a CBOR map; vhlink:/ stays the text form for URI carriers; receivers also accept the string. smart-trust#130 makes the same change on the WHO side.

nodes.label: OI-22
nodes.title: IHE VHL examples break their own rules
nodes.text: The ITI-YY3 example JSON has "extension" but its base64url encodes "extensions". The ITI-YY4 example key is 44 characters and decodes to 33 bytes ("this is a secret key used for enc"), against the 43-character, 32-byte rule stated beside it.
nodes.hint: Fixed in the IHE patch in upstream/ihe-iti-vhl/.

nodes.label: OI-23
nodes.title: trust-phw Health Link payload types exp and v as strings and requires type
nodes.text: HealthLinkPayload types exp and v as string where SMART Health Links and IHE VHL use numbers, and VerifiableHealthLinkPayload makes type 1..1, a field neither SHL nor IHE has.
nodes.hint: Raised as WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust-phw#17: exp integer64, v integer, VHL type 0..1 (absent inside an HCERT).

nodes.label: OI-24
nodes.title: IHE VHL leaves JWE alg/enc non-normative
nodes.text: Document encryption names dir / A256GCM only in an example and defers to "Cryptographic Algorithm Selection", which mandates nothing for encryption (its only baseline is RS256 for signatures). Two conformant implementations need not interoperate. SMART Health Links, which the section cites, fixes dir / A256GCM.
nodes.hint: The library implements dir / A256GCM only and refuses anything else (STT-VHL-007).

nodes.label: OI-25
nodes.title: Manifest URL is List? in one place and List/_search? in another
nodes.text: ITI-YY3 builds the manifest URL as .../List/_search?...; ITI-YY5 shows .../List?... and says the receiver POSTs the parameters to _search. The library accepts both and always POSTs to <base>/List/_search (STT-VHL-005).

nodes.label: OI-26
nodes.title: IHE's Content-Digest example is not RFC 9530 syntax
nodes.text: The ITI-YY5 example sends "Content-Digest: sha-256=X48E...=", but RFC 9530 makes the value a Structured Field byte sequence, "sha-256=:X48E...=:". A sharer verifying strictly rejects the example form. The library emits RFC 9530 syntax (STT-VHL-008).

nodes.label: OI-27
nodes.title: No signed manifest in IHE VHL or SMART Health Links
nodes.text: The journeys ask to "verify DVC and signed VHL manifests against the DEV trust list". Neither specification signs the manifest: the VHL link is signed (the HCERT), and the manifest's integrity rests on mutual TLS and receiver authentication. Either the journey wording changes, or a signed-manifest option is proposed upstream.

nodes.label: OI-28
nodes.title: How a receiver's keyid, and a DID trust list entry, map to keys
nodes.text: ITI-YY5 says keyid is "used to locate key in trust list" but not how; and ITI-YY2's DID trust list is not tied to the COSE kid (8-byte SHA-256 of the DSC) that ITI-YY4 uses to find the VHL signer.

nodes.label: OI-29
nodes.title: $generate-vhl sends the passcode in a GET query string
nodes.text: ITI-YY3's $generate-vhl is a GET with passcode as a query parameter, so the passcode lands in server and proxy logs. Host concern, not the library's; noted for the policy track.
